fatal_errors: The proposed heat-treatment intervention does not reconstruct the high-energy ball milling followed by spark-plasma sintering process.

It omits the target mechanism based on nanocrystalline grain-boundary strengthening, milling-induced lattice strain and dislocation accumulation, densification, and the stabilized 83% FCC/17% BCC phase mixture.
No specific heat-treatment temperature, duration, cooling path, or atmosphere is given, so the intervention is not reproducible.
Short-range order and nanoscale precipitation are treated as interchangeable mediators even though they are structurally distinct and may produce different deformation mechanisms.
The cited evidence does not directly establish that deficient ordering or precipitation controls the properties of CoCrFeNiTi.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the strength–ductility trade-off and offers a generally testable alternative in which ordering or precipitation obstructs dislocations. Its paired baseline/heat-treated comparison, direct structural characterization, mechanical testing, and explicit falsification rule are reasonably discriminating. However, it misses nearly all target-specific processing and structural content: elemental-powder HEBM at 400 rpm and 20:1 ball-to-powder ratio, SPS at 900–1000 °C, nanocrystalline grains below 48 nm, reduced porosity, and the 83% FCC/17% BCC mixture. It also supplies no quantitative predictions corresponding to approximately 675 HV, 1238 MPa yield stress, or 1894 MPa compressive strength. Evidence E1 concerns deformation in an ordered Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni two-phase alloy and only indirectly supports order-mediated slip resistance; E2 concerns CrCoNi/CrMnFeCoNi and does not support the asserted absence-of-order mechanism in CoCrFeNiTi. Thus, the proposal is a plausible but underspecified alternative rather than a reconstruction of the target.
